nvitk.gui.panels.statmodels.column_plot_dialog¶

Distribution viewer for one column of the analysis dataframe.

Description¶

Before fitting anything you want to know what a column looks like: is it bimodal because two territories are pooled, is the tail a real effect or three bad segmentations, does the binning make sense. That is a different question from the model plot, so it gets its own non-modal window — you can leave it open beside the main one and keep changing the plot type or the split.

Interactive throughout: hovering a point names the subject and its territory, which is what turns “there is an outlier” into “sub-0142’s left MCA”.

_plottable_columns() → list[str]¶

Every column worth a distribution — numeric first, then the categoricals.

_split_columns(max_levels: int = _MAX_SPLIT_LEVELS) → list[str]¶

Columns usable as a grouping: discrete, and few enough levels to stay readable.

A numeric column is only offered when it is a Categorical — a continuous measurement has as many “levels” as rows and grouping by it is meaningless. subject_uid is excluded the same way, by the level cap.

_sync_split_choices() → None¶

Repopulate the grouping pickers for the current mode, keeping the selection where possible.

Panels tolerate far more levels than overlaid violins, so the list genuinely differs between modes rather than being one compromise cap.

_hover_columns() → list[str]¶
